references.text: The preceding verse describes the blessing of the servants whom the Lord finds awake when he comes – [ref:Luk 12:37|Luke 12:37] forms the immediate context for verse 38, which extends the promise to apply regardless of which night watch the Lord arrives in.

Jesus emphasizes in [ref:Luk 12:40|Luke 12:40] that the Son of Man will come at a time they do not expect, explaining why the servants must be ready through all night watches, as described in verse 38.

In [ref:Mark 13:35-36|Mark 13:35–36], Jesus mentions the four night watches – evening, midnight, rooster crowing, and morning – and urges the disciples to stay awake, for they do not know when the master of the house will come. This is a close parallel to the idea of the various night watches in Luke 12:38.

[ref:Matt 24:42-44|Matthew 24:42–44] contains the same exhortation to stay awake because one does not know what hour the Lord will come, paralleling Luke 12:38 where it may be the second or third night watch.

In the parable of the ten virgins, it concludes with the call: "Therefore keep awake, for you do not know the day or the hour" ([ref:Matt 25:13|Matthew 25:13]). This supports the same theme as Luke 12:38 – blessed is the one who is ready whenever the bridegroom comes.

Paul writes in [ref:1 Tess 5:2-4|1 Thessalonians 5:2–4] that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, but that believers are not in darkness so that this day should surprise them. This connects to the readiness through the night watches in Luke 12:38.

[ref:1 Pet 1:13|1 Peter 1:13] exhorts to gird up one's mind and be sober, with hope fixed on the grace that will be brought at the revelation of Jesus Christ – a direct parallel to the prepared attitude praised as blessed in Luke 12:38.

In [ref:Åp 16:15|Revelation 16:15], Jesus says: "Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps their garments." This blessing of the one who stays awake mirrors Luke 12:38, where those who are ready regardless of the night watch are called blessed.

The prophet Habakkuk is urged to wait for the vision even if it delays ([ref:Hab 2:1-3|Habakkuk 2:1–3]). Patient, watchful waiting for the Lord's coming – even if it takes time – is the same motif found in Luke 12:38.
